Sound familiar?

The content is strong. The delivery isn’t doing it justice.

  • You know the material inside out, but the key point gets lost in the room.
  • Board updates run long and the message you wanted remembered gets buried.
  • A tough question lands and the answer comes out longer than you meant.
  • On video calls and interviews you come across flatter than you really are.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

How to open so the room leans in

What to say in your first 30 seconds so people listen to the rest.

How to structure any message in three lines

A simple way to plan an update, pitch or briefing so the point survives a short attention span.

How to handle tough questions calmly

Bridging techniques to answer clearly, stay on message and keep your composure.

Voice, pace and pause

The small changes that make you sound more senior, without sounding rehearsed.

Presence on camera

How to come across well on video calls, recorded messages and media interviews.

Live masterclass · £17Sign up

Script 1 · “The first 30 seconds”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Most presentations are decided in the first 30 seconds.”

Body

“On live TV you don’t get a warm-up. You lead with the story, or people switch off. Boardrooms work the same way. Open with your point, not your agenda, and the room stays with you.”

CTA

“I’m teaching exactly how in a live 60-minute masterclass. It’s £17 and the replay is included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera, same setup as your speaking-tips reels.

Script 2 · “The tough question”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Here’s what to do when a question throws you.”

Body

“Don’t rush to fill the silence. Pause, acknowledge the question, then bridge back to the point that matters. It sounds simple. Under pressure, it’s a skill you have to practise.”

CTA

“I’ll walk you through it live in the Broadcast Confidence Masterclass. 60 minutes, £17. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera, on-screen text “pause, acknowledge, bridge” in gold.

Script 3 · “Three lines”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“If you can’t say it in three lines, the room won’t remember it.”

Body

“Headline. Why it matters. What you need from them. That’s it. It works for a board update, a pitch and a media interview, and it stops you over-explaining.”

CTA

“Join my live masterclass and we’ll build yours together. Seats are £17. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a card with the three lines listed.

laoishemaccana Sponsored···
1/8

You know the material. So why does the point get lost in the room?

It’s rarely the content. It’s the delivery.

On live TV there’s no second take. You lead with the story.

Boardrooms work the same way. Open with your point, not your agenda.

Headline. Why it matters. The ask. Three lines.Then pause, and let it land.

Authority is a skill. It has steps. It can be learned.
